notes:
Account summary: HyperFind is building a unified enterprise search product for Fortune 100 clients. Primary pain: unit cost for queries at massive scale (currently planning 100M–1B vectors). They operate hybrid: hot indexes in-region and cold archive.

POC ask / constraints:
- Need a production pathway for 500M vectors in initial POC, planned ramp to 1B+ in 12 months.
- Query profile: mostly short user queries (1–3 tokens prompt) with heavy reranking stage (top 100 -> re‑rank with contextual reranker).
- Throughput target: 2k QPS sustained across peak windows, spiky bursts to 10k QPS.
- Cost sensitivity: target < $0.0005 per query (embeddings + retrieval + rerank) on average across mixed hot/cold traffic.
- Security: must pass SSO + audit logging + EU data residency for some customers. Looking at Private deployment in EU for regulated clients.

Technical preferences / hints from call:
- Currently evaluating IVF+PQ on FAISS vs HNSW + productized reranker. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations: batching, prefix caching, quantization profiles.
- Wants automated fallback routing: hosted -> dedicated -> private depending on region/tenant.
- Emphasis on tail latency control; "we'd rather pay a little more to avoid 500ms spikes". Quote: "No more than 300ms visible latency on search page."

POC plan (agreed):
- Week 0–2: ingest 50M vectors (test ingestion pipeline and storage compaction).
- Week 3–5: run 500M ingestion in dedicated cluster; measure indexing throughput, RAM/SSD tradeoffs, quantized vector recall delta.
- Week 6: run 72h performance run at 2k sustained QPS with simulated user traffic; collect token-level cost & latency traces.
- Deliverable: cost-per-query model + config recommendations (batch size, KV cache TTL, quantization profile) and fallback routing policy.

Sales context / pricing notes:
- Procurement leaning to 12–24 month committed Dedicated contract if POC meets p99 SLA and cost targets.
- Legal has flagged EU residency + data processing addendum; security team will run a deeper questionnaire (see drive link).

Call notes (shorthand):
- 2026-02-14: Intro demo. Attendees: CTO (A. Patel), Eng lead search (M. Roberts), infra lead (S. Chen). They asked about SSD vs NVMe tiers and cold-store lifecycle.
- 2026-02-28: Architecture deep-dive. Priya ran kernel selection talk, discussed quantization tradeoffs.
- 2026-03-02: Security sync. Legal requests DPA + SOC2 artefacts, asked about KMS integration.

Quotes: "If we can hit 0.0004/query at scale with <200ms median, we can pull committed capacity."

- Commercial: draft committed capacity term sheet contingent on 500M POC results.
